description: Every automerge rule below deliberately leaves automergeType at its default, 'pr'.
Do not set it to 'branch'. A branch automerge pushes a Renovate branch with NO pull
request, and a repo whose required status checks trigger on `pull_request` therefore
never reports them on that branch — so branch protection can never be satisfied and
the update rebases nightly, forever. nicgpt lost six branches this way for up to 83
days (renovate/react, renovate/lock-file-maintenance, renovate/provider-runtime,
renovate/nextjs-monorepo, renovate/postcss-8.x, renovate/vitest), and the tell was
the dashboard's 'Pending Branch Automerge' section rather than any failure anywhere.
With 'pr', Renovate merges the PR itself once the branch is green, which works on
protected and unprotected repos alike — platformAutomerge stays off, see its commit.
The security fast-path. Until 2026-08-22 there was none: GitHub vulnerability
alerts were DISABLED on all 11 repos, so Renovate had no data source and could
not raise a security PR at all. A CVE therefore waited for the Monday window like
a cosmetic bump, and the nine `next` CVEs were fixed by a hand-rolled branch.
Alerts were enabled on all 11 repos on 2026-08-22; this block says what happens next.
schedule + minimumReleaseAge are overridden HERE deliberately: the Monday window and
the 7-day soak on next/react are right for routine bumps and wrong for a live CVE.
Auto-merge every minor and patch update, in every manager and every depType
(via PR — see the top-level description for why automergeType stays 'pr').
This replaces three narrower rules: 'dependencies' patch, 'devDependencies'
minor + patch, and an explicit automerge:false that held 'dependencies' minors
for manual review.
WHY BLANKET RATHER THAN ENUMERATED. The replaced rules matched on depType, and
the only depTypes they ever named were npm's two. Everything else fell through
with no automerge rule at any level: github-actions emits 'action', 'workflow',
'uses-with', 'github-runner', 'container' and 'service'; gomod emits 'require'
and 'indirect'; npm itself also emits 'optionalDependencies', 'peerDependencies',
'engines' and 'packageManager'. That is what left el-harness #59, el-website #7,
linear-tui #15 and el-admin #194 sitting open for 8-22 days.
AND WHY ONE RULE RATHER THAN A LONGER LIST. Renovate automerges a BRANCH only
when EVERY update on it qualifies. el-admin #194 carried an automergeable
@types/node patch next to a 'uses-with' row that matched nothing, and the one
unmatched row held the whole branch manual. Enumerating depTypes leaves that
failure exactly one unlisted depType away, forever.
Majors are untouched — the dependencyDashboardApproval rule below still holds
them, and 'digest'/'pinDigest' are deliberately NOT auto-merged here: a moved
tag on an already-pinned SHA is the supply-chain case, not a version bump.

description: GitHub Actions majors auto-merge on ci. Overrides the blanket major rule above
(later packageRules win), restoring EDR-0062 §6's tiering — 'dev/tooling/actions
-> auto-merge on ci; runtime libs -> dependency-gate; majors -> human'. The blanket
rule was holding actions majors too, which the tiering never intended: an actions
bump changes the CI runner, not shipped code, and ci proves it before merge.
GitHub Actions soak for three days before auto-merging, matching the npm soak
this preset already inherits. config:best-practices pulls in
security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, and EVERY rule in that preset is scoped
matchDatasources: ['npm'] — so actions, which resolve through github-tags,
github-releases and github-digest, had no soak at all and would otherwise
auto-merge a release the same hour it is published.
SCOPED BY matchUpdateTypes ON PURPOSE — DO NOT WIDEN IT. The inherited npm
preset carves minimumReleaseAge back to null for lockFileMaintenance, pin,
replacement, bump, lockfileUpdate and rollback, because those update types have
no release timestamp to age against. Later packageRules win, so a blanket
minimumReleaseAge added here would override those carve-outs — and the failure
is silent, not loud: internalChecksFilter defaults to 'strict' and
minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour to 'timestamp-required', so the update is marked
pending and never raised. No PR, no error, just a dashboard section.
minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour IS SET HERE FOR THAT SAME REASON. The github-runners
datasource is a hardcoded list of runner labels and emits no releaseTimestamp
on any of them, so a runs-on bump has nothing to age against and would stall
under the default. 'timestamp-optional' lets it through with a warning while
still soaking every update that does carry a timestamp.
Majors are out of scope deliberately: they are gated by dashboard approval, and
the actions-majors override above is left exactly as it is.
Restates the inherited carve-outs for the surface the rule above covers, so
that widening that rule cannot resurrect the silent stall described in it.
A no-op today — the soak above does not match these update types — and scoped
to github-actions so it cannot reach the npm soak or the next/react soaks.
